dimensions.assessment: Directly affects the Quinault Indian Nation, the U.S. Forest Service, and the Department of the Interior.
dimensions.evidence: approximately 72 acres of specified lands in Washington from the U.S. Forest Service to the Department of the Interior. Interior must take this land into trust for the benefit of the Quinault Indian Nation.

dimensions.assessment: Transfers ownership and administrative status of a specific 72-acre parcel of land into tribal trust.
dimensions.evidence: administratively transferred from the Forest Service to the Department of the Interior and taken into trust for the benefit of the Quinault Indian Nation.

dimensions.assessment: No specific federal spending or revenue amounts are reported, though remediation of hazardous materials is waived.
dimensions.evidence: shall not otherwise be required to remediate or abate those hazardous substances, pollutants, or contaminants.

dimensions.assessment: Applies a specific administrative land transfer and trust designation for a single tribal allotment.
dimensions.evidence: generally depicted as 'Allotment 1157' on the map entitled 'Quinault Indian Nation Land Transfer Act'

dimensions.assessment: Permanent change in land status and reservation boundaries.
dimensions.evidence: The land taken into trust under subsection (a) shall be part of the Quinault Indian Reservation

missing_information: Financial valuation of the 72 acres of land transferred.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill transfers approximately 72 acres of federal land from the Forest Service to the Department of the Interior to be held in trust for the Quinault Indian Nation.
